ex: An echograph records sound echoes as a picture or line.
The ship used an echograph to measure the depth of the sea.
The doctor looked at the echograph image of the heart.
Our lab has an old echograph for testing materials.
Ecocentrism puts nature, not people, at the center of values.
Our ethics class compared ecocentrism with human-centered ideas.
Ecocentrism says rivers and forests have value on their own.
Many green activists support ecocentrism.
An econometrist uses math and statistics to study the economy.
The bank hired an econometrist to forecast prices.
The econometrist built a model of unemployment.
My sister works as an econometrist at a university.
An ecossaise is a fast dance in two-four time.
The pianist played a short ecossaise at the concert.
My piano teacher gave me an easy ecossaise to learn.
People danced the ecossaise at balls in the 1800s.
Ecphrasis is a detailed description of a work of art in a text.
The poem is an ecphrasis of a famous painting.
Our literature teacher explained ecphrasis with an old poem.
Writers use ecphrasis to make a picture come alive in words.
Ecthyma is a skin infection that causes deep sores.
The doctor gave the child antibiotics for ecthyma.
Ecthyma often appears on the legs.
Keep the skin clean to help ecthyma heal.
An ecumenist works for unity between Christian churches.
The ecumenist invited Catholic and Orthodox priests to a meeting.
As an ecumenist, she speaks at many church conferences.
The new bishop is a well-known ecumenist.
Edaphon means all the tiny living things in the soil.
Worms, fungi, and bacteria are part of the edaphon.
Healthy edaphon helps plants grow.
Farm chemicals can harm the edaphon.
In occult ideas, an egregore is a group spirit made by shared thoughts.
The book says every club has its own egregore.
Some writers describe the egregore of a whole nation.
She read about the egregore in a book on magic.
Our city bought a new electrobus for the downtown route.
The electrobus charges at the last stop.
An electrobus is quiet and does not make smoke.
Is this electrobus going to the train station?
An electrodynamometer measures electric current and power.
The engineer connected the electrodynamometer to the circuit.
Students used an electrodynamometer in the physics lab.
This old electrodynamometer still gives correct readings.
An electrograph is a record made by an electric device.
The lab printed an electrograph of the signal.
The scientist studied the electrograph of the leaf.
An electrograph can show small changes in voltage.
The machine sends an electroimpulse to the muscle.
Each electroimpulse lasts less than a second.
The device uses a weak electroimpulse to stop pain.
The engineer measured the strength of the electroimpulse.
electroimpulse.note: Usually "electric pulse" or "electrical impulse" in English.

ex: An electrojet is a strong electric current high in the atmosphere.
The equatorial electrojet flows above the equator during the day.
The electrojet can affect radio signals.
Scientists measure the electrojet with satellites.
Electromassage uses weak electric currents to relax muscles.
The physical therapist gave me ten minutes of electromassage.
Electromassage can help after a sports injury.
Ask your doctor before you try electromassage at home.
In 1900, an electromobile was quieter than a gas car.
The museum shows an early electromobile from 1905.
The electromobile was popular in cities a hundred years ago.
My grandfather collects old ads for the electromobile.
electromobile.note: Old word; today people say "electric car" or "EV."

ex: An electromyograph records the electrical activity of muscles.
The neurologist tested my arm with an electromyograph.
The hospital bought a new electromyograph.
An electromyograph helps doctors find nerve problems.
An electronvolt is a very small unit of energy.
This particle has an energy of one million electronvolts.
Physicists use the electronvolt to describe atoms and particles.
The symbol for electronvolt is eV.
An electrophone is a musical instrument that makes sound with electricity.
The theremin was one of the first electrophones.
The music museum has a room of early electrophones.
Our teacher showed us how an electrophone works.
An electrophore is a simple device that makes static electricity.
The teacher charged the electrophore by rubbing it with wool.
We made an electrophore from a metal plate and plastic.
With an electrophore, you can make small sparks.
An electrophotometer measures the strength of light.
The lab uses an electrophotometer to test water samples.
Put the sample into the electrophotometer and read the result.
The electrophotometer showed that the liquid was very dark.
An electroreceptor senses weak electric fields.
Sharks use electroreceptors to find fish in the sand.
Each electroreceptor is a small organ in the skin.
The platypus has electroreceptors in its bill.
Electrotaxis is the movement of cells toward an electric field.
Skin cells show electrotaxis when a wound heals.
The biologist studied electrotaxis in worms.
Weak current can cause electrotaxis in some bacteria.
An electrotypist makes metal printing plates with electricity.
The old printing shop had two electrotypists.
The electrotypist copied the page onto a copper plate.
My great-grandfather worked as an electrotypist.
An elegist is a poet who writes elegies, sad poems about death.
The young poet became famous as an elegist.
The elegist wrote a poem for his lost friend.
Critics called her the best elegist of her time.
Elementarism is an art style based on simple lines and colors.
The museum has a room about Dutch elementarism.
Elementarism used diagonal lines in abstract paintings.
Our art teacher compared elementarism with cubism.
An elevon is a control surface on the wing of a plane with no tail.
The pilot moved the elevons to turn the jet.
Delta-wing planes often use elevons.
The mechanic checked the left elevon before the flight.
An elicitor is a substance that starts a defense reaction in plants.
The scientist sprayed an elicitor on the tomato leaves.
This elicitor helps plants fight fungus.
Farmers use natural elicitors to protect crops.
Elinvar is an alloy that stays elastic when the temperature changes.
Watch springs are often made of elinvar.
The engineer chose elinvar for the precise instrument.
Elinvar contains iron, nickel, and chromium.
An ellipsograph is a tool for drawing ellipses.
The designer used an ellipsograph to draw an oval mirror.
Our drawing class used a wooden ellipsograph.
The ellipsograph helped him draw a perfect oval.
An eluate is the liquid that comes out of a chromatography column.
The chemist collected the eluate in small tubes.
We tested the eluate for protein.
The eluate was clear and had no color.
Embolite is a mineral made of silver, chlorine, and bromine.
The miners found green embolite in the silver mine.
This embolite sample comes from Chile.
Embolite turns darker in the light.
Old biology books wrote embryon instead of embryo.
In early medical texts, the embryon grows in the womb.
The author describes the embryon of a chicken in an egg.
The poet called the idea the embryon of a great plan.
Emphyteusis is a long-term right to use someone else's land.
The farmer got the land under emphyteusis for ninety-nine years.
Under emphyteusis, you must pay rent and improve the land.
Our law professor explained emphyteusis in Roman law.
An emulsoid is a colloid with liquid particles spread in a liquid.
Gelatin in water forms an emulsoid.
The chemistry book compares an emulsoid and a suspensoid.
An emulsoid can become a gel when it cools.
An emulsor is a machine that mixes oil and water into an emulsion.
The factory uses an emulsor to make mayonnaise.
Clean the emulsor after each batch of cream.
The new emulsor mixes paint faster.
An enanthema is a rash inside the mouth.
The doctor saw an enanthema on the child's palate.
Measles can cause an enanthema before the skin rash.
An enanthema is often a sign of a virus.
Enantiomorphism means two forms are mirror images of each other.
Your left and right hands show enantiomorphism.
Quartz crystals can show enantiomorphism.
The chemistry teacher explained enantiomorphism with models.
Enargite is a dark mineral that contains copper and arsenic.
The mine produces copper from enargite.
Enargite crystals are gray-black and shiny.
The geologist found enargite in the rock sample.
An encephalograph records the electrical activity of the brain.
The nurse put sensors on my head for the encephalograph.
The hospital uses an encephalograph to study sleep.
The encephalograph showed normal brain waves.
An encephaloma is a tumor of the brain.
The scan showed a small encephaloma.
Doctors removed the encephaloma during surgery.
An encephaloma can cause headaches and vision problems.
An encolpion is a small cross or icon worn on the chest.
The bishop wore a gold encolpion.
Archaeologists found a bronze encolpion from the 12th century.
The museum shows an encolpion with a small relic inside.
Encyclopedism is the wish to collect all knowledge in one work.
The age of encyclopedism began in 18th-century France.
His encyclopedism impressed everyone at the university.
The exhibit explains the encyclopedism of the Enlightenment.
An endonym is the name a place or people uses for itself.
Deutschland is the endonym for Germany.
Kyiv is the endonym, and it is now used in English.
Many maps show the endonym next to the English name.
An endoparasite lives inside the body of its host.
Tapeworms are endoparasites of humans and animals.
The vet checked the dog for endoparasites.
This medicine kills endoparasites in cattle.
An endoradiosonde is a small capsule that sends data from inside the body.
The patient swallowed an endoradiosonde to measure stomach acid.
The endoradiosonde sends radio signals to a receiver.
Doctors used an endoradiosonde to check the digestive tract.
Endosmos is the flow of water into a cell through its wall.
In pure water, endosmos makes the cell swell.
The old textbook explains endosmos with a raisin in water.
Endosmos helps plant roots take in water.
An endotheliocyte is a cell that lines the inside of blood vessels.
Damaged endotheliocytes can lead to heart disease.
The researcher grew endotheliocytes in the lab.
Each endotheliocyte is very flat and thin.
An endozoochore is a plant whose seeds are spread by animals that eat them.
Cherry trees are endozoochores because birds eat their fruit.
The seeds of an endozoochore pass through the animal's gut.
The botanist listed every endozoochore in the forest.
An enterosorbent is a medicine that absorbs toxins in the gut.
Activated charcoal is a common enterosorbent.
The doctor gave him an enterosorbent for food poisoning.
Take the enterosorbent two hours before other medicines.
Entomofauna means all the insects of a place.
The entomofauna of this forest includes many rare beetles.
Scientists studied the entomofauna of the river valley.
Pesticides can damage the local entomofauna.
An eolith is a stone that may be a very early tool.
The scientist argued that the eolith was shaped by nature.
The museum shows an eolith found in a gravel pit.
Many experts doubt that eoliths are real tools.
Epanaphora is the repetition of a word at the start of lines.
The speech used epanaphora: every line began with "We will."
Our teacher showed us epanaphora in a famous poem.
Writers use epanaphora to make a text stronger.
An eparch is a bishop in some Eastern churches.
The eparch visited our parish on Sunday.
The new eparch leads the Ukrainian Catholic church in the region.
In Byzantium, an eparch also governed a city.
Epiblema is the outer cell layer of a plant root.
Root hairs grow from the epiblema.
The student looked at the epiblema under a microscope.
The epiblema helps the root absorb water.
An epicanthus is a skin fold over the inner corner of the eye.
Many babies have an epicanthus that disappears later.
The doctor noticed an epicanthus during the exam.
An epicanthus is common in people from East Asia.
An epicheirema is an argument where a premise has its own reason.
The logic teacher wrote an epicheirema on the board.
Each premise in an epicheirema comes with a short proof.
We learned the epicheirema in our rhetoric class.
The epicotyl is the part of a young plant above the seed leaves.
In bean seedlings, the epicotyl grows quickly upward.
The students measured the epicotyl every day.
The first true leaves grow from the epicotyl.
An epidiascope projects pictures and slides onto a screen.
The teacher used an old epidiascope to show maps.
Put the page under the epidiascope and turn on the lamp.
Schools used the epidiascope before digital projectors.
Epididymite is a rare white mineral that contains beryllium.
The museum shows a small epididymite crystal.
Collectors look for epididymite in Greenland.
The geologist identified epididymite in the granite.
Epifauna are animals that live on the surface of the sea floor.
Crabs and starfish are part of the epifauna.
The divers counted the epifauna on the rocks.
Fishing nets can damage the epifauna.
An epigone is a weak follower or imitator of a great artist.
Critics called the young painter a mere epigone.
The famous poet had many epigones but no true students.
He did not want to be just an epigone of his teacher.
Epigonism is copying a great artist without new ideas.
The critic accused the band of epigonism.
Epigonism is common after a big art movement ends.
The writer tried to avoid epigonism in her new novel.
An epigrammatist writes short, clever poems.
The epigrammatist mocked politicians in two-line verses.
As an epigrammatist, he was famous for his sharp humor.
Our library has a book by an ancient Roman epigrammatist.
An epigraphist studies old writing on stone and metal.
The epigraphist read the Latin words on the old stone.
The museum hired an epigraphist to study the coins.
An epigraphist helped date the ancient tomb.
The epilimnion is the warm top layer of water in a lake.
In summer, fish often swim in the epilimnion.
The wind mixes the water in the epilimnion.
We measured oxygen in the epilimnion of the lake.
In algebra, an epimorphism is a surjective homomorphism.
The professor proved that this map is an epimorphism.
Every epimorphism of groups is onto.
We studied epimorphisms in our abstract algebra class.
An episcope projects pictures from books or photos onto a screen.
The teacher put the book under the episcope.
Old schools used an episcope instead of a computer projector.
The image from the episcope was big but a little dark.
An epistyle is the stone beam that rests on top of columns.
The epistyle of the old temple is broken.
The architect added an epistyle above the front columns.
Greek letters are carved on the epistyle.
An episyllogism uses the conclusion of another syllogism as a premise.
In logic class, we built an episyllogism from two simple arguments.
The first argument gives a result, and the episyllogism uses it.
The book shows a chain of a prosyllogism and an episyllogism.
An epithelioma is a tumor of the skin or other epithelium.
The doctor removed a small epithelioma from his face.
Too much sun can lead to an epithelioma.
The biopsy showed that the spot was an epithelioma.
An epizoochore is a plant whose seeds stick to animal fur.
Burdock is an epizoochore because its burrs stick to dogs.
The hiker found epizoochore seeds on his socks.
An epizoochore spreads its seeds when animals walk by.
An epopoeia is a long epic poem about heroes.
The professor called the novel a modern epopoeia.
The ancient epopoeia tells of a long war and a journey home.
Students read parts of the epopoeia in translation.
Epsomite is a natural mineral form of Epsom salt.
White epsomite crystals grow on the cave walls.
Epsomite dissolves easily in water.
The museum has a sample of epsomite from a dry lake.
An epulis is a small lump on the gums.
The dentist found an epulis near my front teeth.
An epulis is usually not dangerous.
The vet removed an epulis from the dog's mouth.
An equilibrist is a performer who balances on a rope or wire.
The equilibrist walked across the wire high above the crowd.
The circus has a famous equilibrist from Kyiv.
The equilibrist balanced on a ball and juggled.
Eremurus is a tall garden plant with long spikes of flowers.
We planted eremurus near the fence.
Eremurus is also called foxtail lily.
The eremurus in our garden blooms in early summer.
Erethism is a condition of extreme nervous irritability.
Mercury poisoning can cause erethism.
Workers with erethism became shy and nervous.
The doctor described the patient's erethism in the report.
An ergograph records the work of a muscle.
The scientist used an ergograph to measure finger strength.
The ergograph showed when the muscle got tired.
Students tested the ergograph in the physiology lab.
An ergonomist designs safe and comfortable workplaces.
The company hired an ergonomist to check our desks.
The ergonomist changed the height of my chair.
An ergonomist can help reduce back pain at work.
Ergosterin is a substance in fungi that turns into vitamin D.
Yeast contains a lot of ergosterin.
When mushrooms get sunlight, ergosterin becomes vitamin D.
The old textbook calls this compound ergosterin.
An eristavi was the governor of a region in old Georgia.
The eristavi ruled the mountain province for the king.
The museum shows the sword of a famous eristavi.
Each eristavi collected taxes and led soldiers.
Erythremia is a disease with too many red blood cells.
Patients with erythremia often have headaches.
The blood test suggested erythremia.
Doctors treat erythremia by removing some blood.
erythremia.note: "Polycythemia vera" is the more common term.

ex: Erythrite is a pink mineral that contains cobalt.
The pink crust on this rock is erythrite.
Miners look for erythrite as a sign of cobalt.
Erythrite crystals look like small purple-pink needles.
erythrite.note: Also an old name for the sweetener "erythritol."

ex: An erythroblast is a young cell that becomes a red blood cell.
Erythroblasts form in the bone marrow.
The blood test showed erythroblasts, which is unusual for adults.
Under the microscope, the erythroblast has a nucleus.
The erythron is all the red blood cells and the cells that make them.
Doctors study the erythron in patients with anemia.
Bone marrow is an important part of the erythron.
The professor explained how the erythron responds to blood loss.
An escarp is the steep inner slope of a defensive ditch.
Soldiers dug an escarp in front of the fort.
The castle's escarp is still steep today.
Enemy troops could not climb the escarp.
Eserine is a drug that comes from the Calabar bean.
The eye doctor used eserine drops to make the pupil small.
Eserine can treat some kinds of poisoning.
The pharmacist stored the eserine in a dark bottle.
An esophagoscope is a tube with a light for looking inside the esophagus.
The doctor used an esophagoscope to find the coin the child swallowed.
The nurse cleaned the esophagoscope after the procedure.
A modern esophagoscope has a small camera.
Esthesis is the ability to feel and sense things.
Some nerve diseases reduce esthesis in the hands.
The doctor tested the patient's esthesis with a soft brush.
The article discusses esthesis and perception.
Estrangelo is an old style of Syriac writing.
The ancient Bible is written in estrangelo letters.
Scholars can read estrangelo in old manuscripts.
The museum shows a stone with estrangelo script.
Etatism is a policy where the state controls the economy.
Turkey followed etatism in the 1930s.
Critics say etatism slows private business.
The economist wrote a book about etatism.
An ethnarch was a ruler of a people or province in ancient times.
The ethnarch ruled under the Roman emperor.
The coin shows the name of a local ethnarch.
In the Ottoman Empire, the patriarch was also an ethnarch for Christians.
Ethnicism is a strong focus on ethnic identity and differences.
The politician was criticized for ethnicism.
Ethnicism can divide a country.
The study looks at ethnicism in local elections.
An ethnolect is a way of speaking used by an ethnic group.
Many young people in the city speak an ethnolect.
The linguist recorded the ethnolect of immigrant families.
An ethnolect can mix words from two languages.
Ethyne is a gas used in welding.
The chemistry teacher showed how ethyne burns.
Ethyne has a triple bond between two carbon atoms.
Workers store ethyne in strong metal tanks.
Euclase is a rare blue or green gemstone.
The jeweler set a small euclase in the ring.
Euclase breaks easily, so cut it carefully.
The museum has a beautiful euclase crystal from Brazil.
Eudemonia means a happy and good life.
Greek philosophers wrote a lot about eudemonia.
For many people, eudemonia comes from helping others.
Eudemonia is more than short pleasure.
Eudemonism says the goal of life is happiness and well-being.
Our ethics class compared eudemonism and duty ethics.
Eudemonism links a good life with good character.
She wrote her essay on ancient eudemonism.
A eudemonist believes happiness is the main goal of life.
As a eudemonist, he values friendship and virtue.
The eudemonist argued that good habits bring happiness.
Many ancient philosophers were eudemonists.
Eudialyte is a red mineral that contains zirconium.
Collectors love eudialyte for its bright color.
The pink stone in this pendant is eudialyte.
Geologists found eudialyte in the old volcanic rocks.
A eudiometer is a glass tube for measuring gas volume.
The chemist collected hydrogen in a eudiometer.
We used a eudiometer in the gas reaction experiment.
Read the gas level on the eudiometer scale.
Euglobulin is a protein that does not dissolve in pure water.
The lab did a euglobulin test to check blood clotting.
Doctors measure euglobulin lysis time in the hospital.
The lab separated the euglobulin from the blood sample.
Euhemerism says myths are stories about real people from long ago.
According to euhemerism, old gods were once kings.
The professor explained euhemerism in our mythology class.
Euhemerism is one way to explain old legends.
A eupatrid was a noble in ancient Athens.
Only a eupatrid could hold high office in early Athens.
The eupatrid family owned much of the land.
The book describes the power of the eupatrids.
Euphuism is a very elaborate and artificial style of writing.
The novel's euphuism makes it hard to read.
Teachers warn students against euphuism in essays.
Euphuism was fashionable in England in the 1580s.
euphuism.note: Not the same as "euphemism" (a polite word for something unpleasant).

ex: A eurocent is one hundredth of a euro.
This candy costs fifty eurocents.
Do you have a five-eurocent coin?
The price of bread went up by ten eurocents.
A euroregion is an area where border regions of two countries work together.
Our town is part of a euroregion with Poland.
The euroregion helps build new roads across the border.
The euroregion runs projects for tourism and culture.
A euryphage is an animal that eats many kinds of food.
Rats are euryphages and can live almost anywhere.
The brown bear is a euryphage.
As a euryphage, this fish eats plants and insects.
A eurypterid was an ancient sea scorpion.
Some eurypterids were longer than a person.
The museum shows a eurypterid fossil.
The kids found a small eurypterid fossil on the beach.
An evaporometer measures how much water evaporates.
The weather station has an evaporometer.
Farmers use evaporometer data to plan watering.
Check the evaporometer every morning.
An exanthema is a skin rash caused by an illness.
Measles causes a typical exanthema.
The child had a fever and an exanthema.
The doctor said the exanthema was from a virus.
An excitron is a mercury-arc rectifier tube.
Old railway power stations used excitrons.
The excitron changes alternating current to direct current.
The engineer replaced the excitron with a modern rectifier.
An exhauster is a fan that removes air, gas, or dust.
The factory installed a new exhauster in the paint room.
Turn on the exhauster before you start welding.
The exhauster pulls smoke out of the kitchen.
The exhumator opened the old grave for the police.
An exhumator needs special permission from the court.
The exhumator worked carefully with the forensic team.
The exhumator moved the remains to a new cemetery.
exhumator.note: Usually "exhumer," or say "the people who exhume the body."

ex: The experimentator wrote down every result.
An experimentator must repeat the test many times.
The experimentator changed the temperature in the lab.
Our chemistry teacher is a careful experimentator.
An explicator is a person who explains a text or idea.
The professor is a careful explicator of difficult poems.
As an explicator, she makes hard texts clear.
The explicator wrote notes for each chapter.
The explorator traveled deep into the jungle.
Each explorator kept a diary of the trip.
The explorator found a new river.
The museum honors the brave explorator.
An expropriator takes property from its owners, often by force.
The new government acted as an expropriator of private land.
The farmers protested against the expropriator.
In the novel, the expropriators take over the factory.
An exsiccator is a closed glass container that keeps samples dry.
Put the crystals in the exsiccator overnight.
The exsiccator has a drying agent at the bottom.
The lab assistant cleaned the exsiccator lid.
An extirpator is a farm tool that cuts weeds below the soil.
The farmer pulled the extirpator behind the tractor.
The extirpator loosens the soil before planting.
The farm museum shows an old wooden extirpator.
extirpator.note: Also means a person who destroys something completely.

ex: She does extraprofessional work for a charity on weekends.
His extraprofessional interests include painting and hiking.
The course covers extraprofessional skills like public speaking.
Teachers often have many extraprofessional duties at school.
extraprofessional.note: In English "extraprofessional" is only an adjective: outside your profession.

ex: An extravasate is fluid that has leaked out of a blood vessel.
The doctor saw an extravasate of blood under the skin.
The scan showed extravasate around the injury.
The nurse found extravasate near the IV in his arm.
An eyalet was a large province of the Ottoman Empire.
The governor of an eyalet was called a pasha.
Each eyalet was divided into smaller districts.
The map shows every eyalet in the 1600s.
Fabianism aims for socialism through slow reforms, not revolution.
The professor explained fabianism and its history in Britain.
Fabianism had a strong influence on British politics.
Her essay compares fabianism and Marxism.
Factice is a rubber-like material made from vegetable oils.
The factory adds factice to rubber to make erasers.
Factice helps make rubber softer.
White factice is used in light-colored rubber goods.
A fagottist plays the bassoon.
The orchestra needs a new fagottist.
The fagottist played a solo in the second part.
My brother studies to be a fagottist at the conservatory.
The falda is a long white robe worn by the pope.
The falda hung down below the pope's other robes.
The museum shows an old silk falda.
Only the pope wears a falda at special ceremonies.
falda.note: In English, a falda is a long white robe worn by the pope.

ex: Falsificationism says a scientific theory must be testable and possibly wrong.
Our philosophy of science course started with falsificationism.
Falsificationism helps separate science from pseudoscience.
Critics of falsificationism say science is more complex.
A fanfaron is a person who boasts loudly.
Nobody believed the fanfaron's stories about his trips.
He acts like a fanfaron at every party.
The fanfaron talked about his money all evening.
A faverolle is a French breed of chicken with feathered feet.
Our neighbor keeps two faverolle hens.
The faverolle has a beard and lays light brown eggs.
Kids love the calm faverolle at the farm.
Favipiravir is an antiviral drug for flu.
The doctor prescribed favipiravir for five days.
Researchers tested favipiravir against new viruses.
Take favipiravir only with a doctor's advice.
A feldsher is a medical worker with less training than a doctor.
In the village, the feldsher treats most patients.
The feldsher came with the ambulance.
My aunt worked as a feldsher in a rural clinic.
feldsher.note: A medical worker in Eastern Europe, similar to a physician assistant.

ex: Felsite is a fine-grained, light-colored volcanic rock.
Ancient people made tools from felsite.
The trail goes over gray felsite cliffs.
The geologist broke a piece of felsite with a hammer.
A femtometer is one millionth of a nanometer.
A proton is about one femtometer across.
Physicists measure atomic nuclei in femtometers.
The symbol for femtometer is fm.

fibrocement.note: Often called "fiber cement" in American English.

ex: A figurant dances in the group, not as a soloist.
She started her ballet career as a figurant.
The theater needs ten figurants for the crowd scene.
Each figurant must learn the group steps.
figurant.note: Means a ballet or stage extra, not a person in a criminal case.

flibustier.note: Old word; "pirate" or "buccaneer" is common. Also "filibuster".

folacin.note: "Folic acid" or "folate" is the common name.
